title: You would think that is a basic football concept. It is the most basic. And yet, look how fans and teams talk and behave. Do you think all teams and fans act as though the regular season is the playoffs? They are. Way less games in a NFL regular season than a NBA or MLB playoffs. It is the playoffs. I’ve been to a ton of regular season and playoff games for various teams. The energy is different. So, obviously my obvious point isn’t obvious to all. And then the actual playoffs being single elimination is a brutality that doesn’t care how hurt your team is. And yet, in the summer, all sorts of couch-sitting predictor people have ridiculous expectations for teams, like the Bills, as though this is easy, a short regular season with different schedule strengths and any team able to win, leading to brutal single elimination games. One of the best reality programs in the world.

title: Jalen Hurts Training Camp Stats, Day 5: Tuesday was one of the most choppy, discombobulated practices I’ve ever covered The offense performance was filled with backups and flags. Both Devonta Smith and Makai Lemon missed practice due to hamstring injuries. Lane Johnson was once again an excused absence Add in a decision by the coaching staff to have a few periods with (basically) an entire backup offensive line and there were stretches of practice where Jalen Hurts was on the field with 9 or 10 players that weren’t on the team last season Those factors have to go into account when judging Hurts day. He had two nice completions to Wicks, one of which was on third down vs Quinyon. It does seem like Wicks and Hurts are starting to develop some nice chemistry. Because of all the flags (I counted at least seven) the offense really never got going. The 6/19 has to be one of the lowest days I’ve ever charted, but it wasn’t really Hurts fault. His interception was probably a poor decision though as he threw it deep to Hollywood Brown who was double covered. It was picked off by Michael Carter. The offense did get into the end zone once on a throw from Hurts to Brown from about 5-yards out but it was called back due to an illegal formation. Overall it was a day that could have some benefit as Hurts got lots of reps with lots of backups. On the other hand it is probably a day Hurts won’t want to repeat anytime soon. Day 5 Stats: 6/19, 0 TD, 1 INT 2026 Stats: 60/91, 3 TD, 2 INT Grade: C+

The offense performance was filled with backups and flags. Both Devonta Smith and Makai Lemon missed practice due to hamstring injuries. Lane Johnson was once again an excused absence 

Add in a decision by the coaching staff to have a few periods with (basically) an entire backup offensive line and there were stretches of practice where Jalen Hurts was on the field with 9 or 10 players that weren’t on the team last season

His interception was probably a poor decision though as he threw it deep to Hollywood Brown who was double covered. It was picked off by Michael Carter. 

The offense did get into the end zone once on a throw from Hurts to Brown from about 5-yards out but it was called back due to an illegal formation. 

Overall it was a day that could have some benefit as Hurts got lots of reps with lots of backups. On the other hand it is probably a day Hurts won’t want to repeat anytime soon.

title: “I love the Dolphins and the people here, but after 13 years it was just the right time for me to make this decision,” said Garfinkel in a statement. “The business has never been in a better place and the team of people we have here is second to none in sports. I want to thank the South Florida community and Dolphins fans for all of their support over the years and especially Steve Ross for the opportunity to be a part of this great organization. He is a visionary leader and a team owner who always strives to be best-in-class, and he provides his people all the trust and resources needed to be successful. title: Dennis Allen was asked about expectations for several players who will be stepping into new/unfamiliar roles with injuries at nickel and safety. To sum it up, this was as fired up as I've seen him answer any one question in awhile. Allen: "I just want to…everybody asks, ‘What do you want to see out of this guy? What do you want to see out of this guy? What do you want to see out of this guy?’ You know what I want to see? I want to see 11 frickin’ dudes on the field competing their ass off. And if we all do that, then I feel pretty confident that we’ll get them to the right spot. But that’s what this time of year is all about. This is about developing the culture and the way that you’re going to play. That’s what I want to see out of all of them. I want to see it out of the frickin’ 10 year vet, I want to see it out of the rookie."

I want to see 11 frickin’ dudes on the field competing their ass off. And if we all do that, then I feel pretty confident that we’ll get them to the right spot. But that’s what this time of year is all about. This is about developing the culture and the way that you’re going to play. That’s what I want to see out of all of them. I want to see it out of the frickin’ 10 year vet, I want to see it out of the rookie."

During zone, the defender's to this side -- do I put it a way to maximize run after catch? He has the ability to pinpoint the ball into the right location. He has always had that trait. Now in a new system, can he elevate that further? That's the command I'm looking for from those spots. That's the thing, right now, that's so impressive to me. "There was a deep ball to Terry (McLaurin) that was completed just in the best location that went over Mike (Sainristil) and into that location. That's not luck. That's super hard to do. title: There are almost endless reasons why Bijan Robinson deserves this record breaking deal. No one had forced or created more missed tackles or plays over 10 yards last season. He had more scrimmage yards over the last two years than anyone. Or that he's an offensive weapon, not a RB. But if you ask coaches, it's that he's an eraser. Any mistake within a play from the call to a block can be erased by Bijan and he can still find a way to not only create positive yardage, but an explosive play. That's the rarest of rare and he has it.
